title: Caprini Score (Surgical VTE Risk)
sources: Caprini JA. Dis Mon 2005 (2005 checklist, as reproduced by Queensland Health); Lobastov K et al. JVS Venous 2022 (4-tier scheme across 2005/2010/2013); StatPearls (Caprini score, 2013 model prophylaxis mapping)

changelog.change: Rebuilt to the full 2005 Caprini checklist and the 0–1 / 2 / 3–4 / ≥5 four-tier scheme per Calculator_Logic_Build_Spec.md.

purpose: Stratifies perioperative venous-thromboembolism risk for a surgical patient and sets the prophylaxis strategy (mechanical vs. pharmacologic, and its duration). Full 2005 checklist; sum all applicable points. The medical-inpatient counterpart is the Padua score — weigh the result against the surgical bleeding risk before starting pharmacologic prophylaxis.

options.label: None, or a minor procedure not planned
Arthroscopic surgery; OR laparoscopic surgery > 45 min; OR major open surgery > 45 min

items.label: History of major surgery (> 45 min) within the last month
Within the last month — hip/pelvis/leg fracture, multiple trauma, acute spinal cord injury with paralysis, or stroke (count each: 5 points each)

Thrombophilia — Factor V Leiden, prothrombin 20210A, elevated serum homocysteine, lupus anticoagulant, elevated anticardiolipin antibodies, HIT, or other congenital/acquired thrombophilia (count each: 3 points each)
Immobilising plaster cast within the last month
Medical patient currently at bed rest
Congestive heart failure within the last month
Serious lung disease, including pneumonia, within the last month
Oral contraceptives or hormone replacement therapy
History of unexplained stillbirth, recurrent (≥ 3) spontaneous abortion, premature birth with toxaemia, or growth-restricted infant

interpretation.label: Low risk — early ambulation is generally sufficient; pharmacologic or mechanical prophylaxis not routinely required
Moderate risk — mechanical prophylaxis (intermittent pneumatic compression); pharmacologic prophylaxis may be considered based on clinical context and bleeding risk
High risk — pharmacologic prophylaxis (LMWH / low-dose UFH) recommended during hospitalisation, with mechanical methods added if appropriate

Highest (very high) risk — combined pharmacologic AND mechanical prophylaxis, often with extended pharmacologic prophylaxis after discharge (7–10 days); a score > 8, or major cancer / orthopaedic surgery, may warrant up to ~30 days

notes: This is the 2005 checklist. The 2013 revision adds further items (smoking, insulin-dependent diabetes, chemotherapy, blood transfusion, surgery > 2 h, additional female-specific factors) — not included here. Always weigh the score against the surgical bleeding risk (and, in medical inpatients, the IMPROVE bleeding score) before committing to pharmacologic prophylaxis.
buildNote: Full 2005 Caprini checklist, additive. 4-tier scheme 0–1 / 2 / 3–4 / ≥5 per Lobastov 2022; prophylaxis text per the 2013 StatPearls mapping. 5-point and multi-thrombophilia rows use count-each option groups.
